claims.claim_text: The indexed Jean Morere is a high-confidence match to Jean-Marie Morère, founder of the OSS-linked Wi-Wi network.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The French military archive supplies an individual network-agent dossier, while independent histories connect Jean-Marie Morère to the OSS Wi-Wi network and Marseille police.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive name, French OSS network context, archived agent dossier, and matching officer-level role; the index rank and later captain title are preserved separately.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources place police service before resignation in March 1943 and OSS contact around May 1943.
claims.match_notes: The printed index spelling and Lt rank remain unchanged. Jean-Marie Morère, Mor, and Pierre Vidal are documented variants; a later history calls him captain.

sources.locator_override: Origins and chronology of the Wi-Wi network

claims.claim_text: Jean-Marie Morère served in the Marseille police from 1 May 1921 until resigning in March 1943, his last documented civilian employment before OSS contact.
claims.evidence_excerpt: entré dans la police de Marseille le 1er Mai 1921
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Two independent historical accounts state that Morère entered the Marseille police on 1 May 1921 and resigned in March 1943 before traveling to Spain and meeting American intelligence representatives.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence through the official French agent dossier and distinctive Wi-Wi network chronology linked to the indexed name.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the last documented civilian employer; not labeled immediate because resignation and travel intervened before OSS contact.
claims.match_notes: The claim distinguishes last civilian employer from immediate pre-OSS affiliation and does not infer unemployment or formal Free French assignment during the intervening weeks.
